events.title: Harold Godwinson crowned King of England
events.description: The day after Edward the Confessor's death, Harold was crowned, probably in Westminster Abbey. William of Normandy disputed the succession and invaded that autumn, killing Harold at Hastings.
events.html: The day after Edward the Confessor's death, Harold was crowned, probably in Westminster Abbey. William of Normandy disputed the succession and invaded that autumn, killing Harold at Hastings.

events.title: Philip of Swabia is crowned a second time at Aachen
events.description: Philip of Swabia, elected King of the Romans in 1198, was crowned again at Aachen, the traditional coronation site, by the Archbishop of Cologne, his former opponent. The repeated ceremony cleared the taint of his first coronation.
events.html: Philip of Swabia, elected King of the Romans in 1198, was crowned again at Aachen, the traditional coronation site, by the Archbishop of Cologne, his former opponent. The repeated ceremony cleared the taint of his first coronation.

events.title: Joan of Arc is born at Domrémy
events.description: By tradition Joan of Arc was born on Epiphany in the village of Domrémy, in north-eastern France. She led French forces to relieve Orléans in 1429, was burned in 1431 and canonised in 1920.
events.html: By tradition Joan of Arc was born on Epiphany in the village of Domrémy, in north-eastern France. She led French forces to relieve Orléans in 1429, was burned in 1431 and canonised in 1920.

events.title: Alfred Vail and Samuel Morse demonstrate their telegraph
events.description: At the Speedwell Ironworks in New Jersey, Vail and Morse sent messages over two miles of wire using an early form of their code. Telegraph lines soon spread across America and the world.
events.html: At the Speedwell Ironworks in New Jersey, Vail and Morse sent messages over two miles of wire using an early form of their code. Telegraph lines soon spread across America and the world.

events.title: Maria Montessori opens her first Casa dei Bambini
events.description: In a tenement in Rome's San Lorenzo district, Montessori opened a 'children's house' for working families. The child-led methods she developed there spread to schools across the world.
events.html: In a tenement in Rome's San Lorenzo district, Montessori opened a 'children's house' for working families. The child-led methods she developed there spread to schools across the world.

events.title: Alfred Wegener presents his theory of continental drift
events.description: At a geology meeting in Frankfurt, Wegener argued that the continents had once formed a single landmass and drifted apart. Long rejected, the idea was vindicated by plate tectonics in the 1960s.
events.html: At a geology meeting in Frankfurt, Wegener argued that the continents had once formed a single landmass and drifted apart. Long rejected, the idea was vindicated by plate tectonics in the 1960s.

events.title: Roosevelt sets out the 'Four Freedoms'
events.description: In his State of the Union address, Franklin Roosevelt named freedom of speech, freedom of worship, freedom from want and freedom from fear as universal rights. The speech shaped Allied war aims and the UN.
events.html: In his State of the Union address, Franklin Roosevelt named freedom of speech, freedom of worship, freedom from want and freedom from fear as universal rights. The speech shaped Allied war aims and the UN.

events.title: Britain recognises the People's Republic of China
events.description: The United Kingdom became the first major Western power to recognise Mao Zedong's communist government in Beijing. The decision, partly aimed at protecting Hong Kong, split Britain from US policy.
